A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GABI research work. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original GABI reconstruction and uncertainty-quantification experiments on heat, airfoil, car-resonance, and terrain problems, including additional analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including Tables 1–5 and reconstruction figures.

M1.justification: The geometry-conditioned autoencoder, MMD training objective, ABC/NUTS inference, and observational-noise estimation remain unchanged. The GCN, GEN, and Transformer implementations were already present in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same heat, airfoil-flow, car-resonance/source-localization, and terrain-flow tasks. Known/unknown-noise scenarios and the out-of-distribution airfoil evaluation in Appendix B.4.2 are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–5 retain the same comparator membership within each experiment, including Direct Map variants and graph GPs with Matérn 1/2, Matérn 3/2, and RBF kernels. The ABC/NUTS and GCN/Transformer comparisons are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same training budgets, model configurations, preprocessing, observation sampling, noise settings, inference budgets, and metrics. Correcting the Adam citation does not change the reported optimizer.

E4.justification: The latent-dimension and channel-size analyses in Figures 8–9, architecture comparison in Table 5, and out-of-distribution airfoil test in Figure 13 are unchanged. The reconstruction and prior-sampling examples are also retained.

E5.justification: The MAE plus/minus reporting, posterior coverage percentages, and plotted error bars are unchanged. Both versions retain the page 8 footnote specifying 100 GABI-NUTS runs instead of 1,000; no seed or statistical-estimation changes appear.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the plotted results retain the same values and findings. For example, GABI-ABC heat MAE remains 1.58e-2 in Table 1, and airfoil pressure MAE remains 6.92e-2 in Table 3. Appendix ablation and out-of-distribution results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemma 2.1, Theorem 2.2, Corollary 2.3, their Appendix A proofs, and the Appendix C formulations retain their mathematical content. Section 1.3 makes sample indices consistent, and Appendix A.3 corrects grammar without changing the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, five introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about geometry-aware priors, observation-independent training, posterior equivalence, predictive accuracy, uncertainty quantification, and scalability.

C2.justification: The interpretations of uncertainty, architecture efficiency, and prior samples remain unchanged. Appendix B.4.2 retains the same limited-robustness qualification for out-of-distribution geometries, and Appendix C retains the same arguments about VAE applicability.

D1.justification: V4 adds an explicit GABI code-repository link to the first-page footnote; v2 supplies no such pointer. Other implementation and hardware details remain unchanged. Repository contents and usability cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. The malformed Adam reference and its in-text citations are corrected to Kingma and Ba, retaining the same title, year, and arXiv identifier; this is a bibliographic correction.

P1.justification: V4 makes scattered spelling, grammar, punctuation, hyphenation, and notation-consistency corrections throughout the main text and appendices. The section organization and narrative remain intact, with no extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: Caption corrections include 'Unkown' to 'Unknown' in Table 2, 'ampltitude' to 'amplitude' in Figure 4, and 'Lose' to 'Loss' in Figure 7. The first-page footnote and bibliography have small layout changes; figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Relative to v2, v4 improves resource discoverability through the new code pointer and modestly improves clarity through language, notation, and citation corrections. The scientific evidence, theory, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited. The PDFs alone do not establish code completeness or executability.
